lines.en: The worst that could happen is that she turns into an unrecognizable Lovecraftian horror who tears my limbs from my body and uses secretions from her tongue to dissolve my torso and pelvic area.
But I’m sure nothing like that will happen because this isn’t that type of story.
This is a redemption tale of Kumon-mi’s most hideous individual — a man who goes from predator to parent. And I’m glad that I have someone like you to tag along for the ride with me.
Because as I stare past this potential demon and in through the windows of suburban homes as they zoom past us, I realize it’s going to be a long one.
I also realize that I must have left the better me at the bus stop as I can, once again, not help but be swallowed by the metaphorical quicksand that is my permanently indeterminate mental state.
The difference this time is that no one is in danger but me.
It’s because I feel like there is something else on the bus.
It’s because I feel like we’re being followed.
And I can not figure out whether I want to shield this tiny creature with my own body or lift her up and offer her as a sacrifice to whatever unknown entity wants to crawl inside of me.
Please find peace in her instead — as she is far more pure than I will ever be.
Just kidding.
Nao is my responsibility until the end of the day.
And I will never let anything bad happen to her.
For if I did, I’d never stop regretting it.
I don’t know why I feel this way.
I just know that I do.
: Are you hungry?
: I’m going to take that as a yes.
: In hindsight, I probably should have thought a little harder about dragging you around all day without feeding you since I’m pretty sure that’s supposed to be my responsibility as well.
: To be fair though, some of it falls on you for not reminding me or asking for food at any point.
: Yes, I know you’re incapable of speaking. But you could have pointed at one of the hundred food stalls or cafes we passed in the mall.
: Yeah, well...now you know for next time.
: Just out of curiosity, what happens if you try to speak?
: Like...what happens if you open your mouth and try to...make noise come out of it? Have you attempted that at all?
: I know Kaori’s trying to teach you how to read at the moment, but developing some way to communicate vocally would probably be a little more useful than that, don’t you think?

: At the very least, it’d be polite to try. Not being able to talk isn’t just an inconvenience to you, but everyone else as well. There are only so many signs you can hold up to convey how you’re feeling.
: Yes, I know. You regret leaving your notebook behind.
: What? Why are you pointing at me?
: Is it because I was able to understand you without any signs at all? And how me doing that is somehow a testimony to how little you actually need real speech in order to get by?
: You know, maybe this isn’t so difficult after all? The more time I spend with you, the easier it becomes to just sort of understand what you want.
: It would still be cool if you tried, though.
: Do you...not want to speak?
: Mouth?
: Ahh...so you can’t make any noise even if you want to, huh?
: I guess it can’t be helped then. Maybe your...vocal cords just need to grow in or something first? I have no idea how your mysterious Lovecraftian body works.
: Don’t worry about it. Instead, why not just try signing out what type of food you want to eat? I’m not really hungry, so anything you want is probably fine.
: On second thought, I don’t think this is going to work.
: Why don’t we just stop for ramen? It’s quick and cheap and I feel suddenly compelled to go there for reasons I am not quite sure of.
: Are you trying to tell me that’s what you were signing?
: Because...noodles are long? That’s what that hand gesture was?
: Your gesturing could use some work too.
Against my better judgement, I escort a child to the second half of town.
It’s the last place I should be taking her and I am fully aware of that, but I cave into this bizarre craving for the thickest, most pungent air because it is what my lungs need.
Exhausted and light-headed due to a day’s worth of untainted inhalation, the dreadmist of the Old District rescues me from feelings I struggle to properly convey to you.
But being unable to properly convey feelings is a major theme in this wretched world of ours. And it’s made even more prevalent by a young girl who fully embodies this.
Perhaps that is what she is — the physical manifestation of something I’ve had a half-hearted grip on...sent down or up from heaven or hell to serve as a visual reminder of this concept’s importance.
If no one understands you, no one will ever love you.
And if no one ever loves you, it will be impossible to understand anything.
The escort goes well — and the child arrives at Tojo Ramen with her estimated innocence still intact.
And I arrive with yet another burden.
: Welcome to Tojo Ramen. Please let me know if you have any questions about the menu.
: No questions, Tsuneyo.
: In that case, may I ask one?
: This is Nao. She’s a...friend of a friend.
: Is that so?

: Then...Nao, if you have any questions about the menu or would like a recommendation, please let me know. I am the acting proprietor and resident flavor samurai. Those who doubt my power will be destroyed.
: I am only kidding.
: You may take a seat wherever you like, but I recommend the spot in the corner. It’s the closest to the fan and you’ll be able to watch me work from there.
: Does that sound interesting to you?
: Excellent choice. Please take a moment to look over the menu. I will take your order momentarily.
: You’re...surprisingly good with kids, Tsuneyo.
: I simply excel in customer service. It’s no more or less than that.
: Tsuneyo, could I...maybe get a box for my food? I’m running a little late for...stuff.
: Absolutely not. What kind of establishment do you think this is, you ungrateful harlot?
: Yeah...should’ve seen that coming.
: Hey, Noriko. Are you just getting out of work?
: I’m...off tonight. I just came by to...strategize with Tsuneyo for the...contest thing.
: Do you mind if I sit next to you?
: Uhh...no. No, that’s fine. It’s not like I...own the counter or anything.
Noriko begins to uncomfortably shift around in her seat as I take my place beside her...and I’m not going to pretend I don’t understand why.
The two of us have barely even made eye contact since Ami interrupted us in my bedroom.
I don’t blame her for that, of course. It was my fault for being unable to push my niece away...and if she needs more time to get back to normal with me, so be it.
I’m not about to rush her when I told her to her face that I need her to suffer in order for me to live a better life.
But I’m also not about to let the two of us drift any further away...so please excuse me while I attempt to reestablish some sort of status quo.
: Noriko-
: So! You’re a...babysitter now? Or did you...maybe get back into tutoring during your free time or...or something?...
: Like I said, she’s a friend of a friend. Or a relative. Or a daughter of a friend. Whichever one is easiest to rationalize inside of your head.
: Hahah. Funny joke — implying that I’ve been able to rationalize literally anything at all lately.
: Still think it’s best that we spend a little time apart?
: Not even sure if we can with how my Dorm Wars contest is gonna work...
: How is that going to work, by the way? Because I’m not sure I even understand.

: Neither are we, but...I think the goal is to just...get past your bodyguards and sort of “capture” you. Kind of like a capture the flag type thing, just...you’re the flag and we don’t need to take you back home.
: Only issue with that is if we don’t finish that competition early, we might get stuck watching you all weekend long. Which...might create some issues.
: For me, definitely. I think you’d be pretty good at that, though. You’ve got more experience watching me than anybody, don’t you?
: I missed out on a few years since you’re an asshole, but...yeah.
: I do...
: Can we start over?
: Like...not from the beginning, obviously. But from right before I went over to your house. That way, we could-
: That’s not a good idea.
: It’s...not?
: No, because it would mean forgetting everything you learned and everything we talked about that night. And even if that was painful for you, it’s important if we’re ever going to move forward.
: I will say, though...it’s been kind of shitty not having you around.
: Imagine how I feel...
: You’re the one keeping her distance. I’m ready to start hanging out with you again whenever you want.
: Maybe...after the Dorm Wars. I just need a little more time to get my head straight and stuff. But the contest might be a good chance for me to do that.
: I really...wasn’t expecting you to show up tonight. It threw my game off hard.
: Well, I’ve been repeatedly throwing you off your game ever since you walked back into my life. So at least you’re starting to get used to it.
: Yeah...
: At least there’s that...
And I arrive to be greeted by at least one concerned expression.
: Whaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaat?
: Welcome to Tojo Ramen. Please let me know if you have any questions about the menu.
: No questions, Tsuneyo.
: In that case, may I ask one?
: This is Nao. She’s a...friend of a friend.
: Is that so?

: Then...Nao, if you have any questions about the menu or would like a recommendation, please let me know. I am the acting proprietor and resident flavor samurai. Those who doubt my power will be destroyed.
: I am only kidding.
: You may take a seat wherever you like, but I recommend the spot in the corner. It’s the closest to the fan and you’ll be able to watch me work from there.
: Does that sound interesting to you?
: Excellent choice. Please take a moment to look over the menu. I will take your order momentarily.
: You’re...surprisingly good with kids, Tsuneyo.
: I simply excel in customer service. It’s no more or less than that.

: Sorry...did nobody hear me when I said, “Whaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaat?” Because I can’t be the only one who wants a little more of an explanation for this mystery girl than “She’s a friend of a friend.”
: Then allow me to explain. Is this seat taken?
: I don’t know. Do you have a friend of a friend of a friend who will be joining us as well? Or maybe a cousin of a distant uncle’s gardener’s pool boy?
: I do, but they won’t be here for another thirty minutes.
: Oh, what luck. That means they’ll be showing up at the same time as my lawn guy’s nephew’s friend’s grandma and her talking platypus.
: I’m very excited to meet them.
: Sensei, who is that really? And why do her eyes look like a cross between Ami’s and Maya’s?
: Because they are. And also, she’s a random girl I found in an alleyway with another friend of mine who went on to adopt her.
: Just what in the 90’s romance anime hell is going on here?
: It’s insane, yes. Though, I’m a little surprised to see you just chalk it up to that and shrug it off.
: You know, after our close closet call the other day, I’m not sure if anything’s going to surprise me anymore.
: Frankly, I’m still kind of creeped out by all of that. But I’m okay with chalking it up to just Ami being a borderline psychopath for now.
: That’s probably for the best.
: What brings you over here, though? Are you working tonight?
: Mhm. My shift’s in about an hour. I just came here to strategize with Tsuneyo since she’ll be my “teammate” for the Dorm Wars this year.
: How is that going to work, by the way? Because I’m not sure I really understand what the deal with that competition is.

: Neither are we, but...I think the goal is to just get past your bodyguards and sort of “capture” you. Kind of like a capture the flag type thing, just...you’re the flag and we don’t need to take you back home.
: Only issue with that is if we don’t finish that competition early, we might get stuck watching you all weekend long. Which...might create some issues.
: For me, definitely. I think you’d be pretty good at that, though. You’ve got more experience watching me than anybody, don’t you?
: Yup! You know me! Destined to chase after you for the rest of eternity instead of being the best Noriko I can be!
: I’m fine with a worse Noriko. The best one might be a little too good and it would only make everyone else jealous.
: I’ll be sure to repeatedly tell myself that the next time I get stuck in a closet.
: I like your shirt.
: Have you decided what you’d like to eat, Nao?
: House specialty tonkotsu ramen...okay.
: You understand her too, Tsuneyo?
: Of course. I can tell what anyone wants to eat by simply looking at them.
: Then...why do you always ask?
: Because it is the right thing to do. Now shut your mouth and let me converse with this child.
: Nao, I take it you are not from around here?
: You look awfully comfortable. Most people with knowledge of this area are rather cautious when it comes to entering establishments such as this one.

: Which would mean you either don’t understand where you are...or you understand it even better than I do. And seeing as I have been here my entire life, I’m quite sure it would have to be the former.
: Forgive me. I’m sure I’m boring you when you would just like to eat.
: But...

: Actually, remain there. It’s not often younger girls enter Tojo Ramen, but...I believe there is something stashed away from years past that may be of some use to you when it comes to keeping you busy.
: If you do not like it, please feel free to throw it back in my face. Thank you.
: Here — a small assortment of colored mechanical pencils and a suspiciously stiff sheet of paper for you to draw upon. Please scribble to your leisure while I prepare your meal.
: There is no need to thank me. But I will accept a five star review on an Internet outlet of your choosing. It does help.
: Wow...Tsuneyo’s in, like...mom mode right now. I’ve never seen this out of her before.
: You should have seen Chika earlier. She was legitimately about to kidnap her.
: And that’s saying a lot since Chika’s already got one kid she’s taking care of, right?
: Yeah, but...when did you learn about Chinami?
: Long time ago. Chika mentioned something about her sister being really into Niki and I wound up getting her an autograph.
: I don’t mean to rain on your parade, but that autograph was probably for Chika. She’s kind of obsessed with your sister.
: I’m aware. It’s not the first time someone’s pulled that on me. Being the little sister of a famous idol comes with a fair share of stuff like that. You learn to deal with it.
: Isn’t Chika obsessed with you too, though? Does she, like...somehow not know about your history with Nee-san?
: I tried to tell her once but she wasn’t even remotely close to believing me.
: Did you offer to call her? Niki loves when you call her just to show off to people, you know. It doesn’t piss her off at all and you should totally keep doing it.
: I know you’re being sarcastic, but I will continue to do it anyway because it’s funny.
: Hey, as long as you’re not-
: Wait, holding that thought. Your friend’s friend looks like she wants to show you her drawing.
: Cool, Nao...But what is it?
: It’s a sweet album cover, that’s what it is.
: I believe she wants you to tell her you are proud of her.
: Nao, whenever you are done showing your drawing to this horrible man, your food is ready.
: What the hell, Tsuneyo? You haven’t even taken my order yet.
: You are not going to order. You aren’t hungry. I can sense it because I have noodle vision.
: Good job, Nao...
: I’m very proud of you.
After running back to the counter to eat her ramen, Nao handed her drawing off to Tsuneyo so she could pin it to the fridge in the back.
It wasn’t just a kind gesture either. It seemed like Tsuneyo genuinely liked the picture for...whatever reason someone could possibly like something like that.
But either way, it made Nao happy.
And with new clothes covering the outside of her body and noodles covering the inside of it, it is safe to say that my job as a babysitter is now complete-
And that I can finally bring her back to Kaori’s apartment and return home to sleep or masturbate or something.
Probably both. But it would be polite to wait until I’m outside of this restaurant and no longer watching Nao to start thinking about the next time I’m going to touch my penis.
: Did you have a good time, Nao-chan? Isn’t Tsuneyo’s ramen the best?
: Thank you for coming to Tojo Ramen.
: Please do not return again unless you bring Nao. Thank you.
: You’re all taking to her way too quickly. She can’t even talk.
: She doesn’t need to. One simply needs to observe Nao to understand Nao. It’s something you will never understand.
: I...guess not.
: But I should probably be getting her home now, so...say goodbye, Nao.
: Bye-bye, Nao-chan! Have a good night and make sure to hold Sensei’s hand on the way home!
: Goodbye, Nao. Make sure to do the exact opposite of what Noriko just said. Barring the “good night” portion, of course.
: Okay. Thanks, Tsuneyo. Come on, Nao. Time to get you home.
A solemn thing—it was—I said— \nA woman—white—to be—
And wear—if God should count me fit— \nHer blameless mystery—
A hallowed thing—to drop a life \nInto the purple well—
Too plummetless—that it return—
Eternity—until—
: Well, Nao...It’s been real. But the time has come for me to go be an adult somewhere.
: Even if...there’s not much time left for me to be an adult since you consumed my entire Saturday.
: I texted Kaori on the way and she should be back soon. But she said you should have a key and that it’s fine if you’re alone for a little while.
: She also wanted me to ask if you could feed John, but I’m not going to do that because it might be dangerous for you to go anywhere near him at this point in his...growth.
: Yeah...I’ll keep that in mind.
: You know-
: The more I think about it, the more I want to ask you...
: That...
: That drawing.
: What was that?
: Like...was it just a thing you came up with? Or...
: Well, if it wasn’t something you came up with, then what-
